title: Every stage skill carries its purpose, method, next activity, delegations and boundaries from the canonical definition
statement: Each canonical stage definition in `stages/*.json` declares its purpose, its method, its rules for selecting the next question or activity, its allowed delegations with the capabilities each requires, its mutation boundary, its approval boundary and its expected completion summary, and each generated `kiln-stage-<stage-id>` skill carries those seven from its definition. None of them is supplied by the generator's templates or inferred from another field - in particular a stage's purpose is not taken from `producesProse`, which describes its outputs. The generator refuses a definition that lacks a required field rather than filling it in, and the check fails, naming the skill, when any generated field no longer matches its definition.
notes: ⚠️ DEFERRED FROM TSK-0046 ON PURPOSE (O1 and F88, 2026-09-13). TSK-0046 promised these seven, and no canonical definition carries any of them: `stages/*.json` has a name, a decision owner, outputs and exit criteria, and nothing else. A generator asked to emit them would have to write them into its own templates or borrow another field, which recreates exactly the drift CMP-0033 exists to prevent - two descriptions of one pipeline, each invisible from the other. So the definitions gain the fields first, and generation follows. ⚠️ PURPOSE WAS NEARLY BORROWED (F88). The first generator printed `producesProse` under Purpose. That field describes outputs; relabelling it is inference by another route, and it is refused for the same reason a template default is. ⚠️ A TEMPLATE DEFAULT IS A FAILURE, NOT A CONVENIENCE. A skill that says 'delegate as appropriate' because its definition was silent reads exactly like one whose definition said so; refusing the definition is the only way the gap stays visible. ⚠️ THE SPLIT, STATED EXACTLY (corrected 2026-09-20, D50-D56). The earlier wording said delegations and the mutation boundary both "name roles, not rules", which is true of one and misleading about the other. Three separate authorities apply. (1) DELEGATION ROLES AND CAPABILITIES ARE CHECKED AGAINST THE SPECIALIST CONTRACTS. A delegation declares `role` and `capabilities` independently; the loader validates the role against `ROLES` and requires the declared capabilities to equal `contractFor(role).requiredCapabilities`, sorted and unique. It never derives or replaces them, so a definition and a contract that disagree are a refusal rather than a silent rewrite. A role whose contract requires nothing declares `"capabilities": []` explicitly, and a stage that delegates nowhere declares `"delegations": []`. (2) CREATION AUTHORITY REMAINS `produces`, AND THE MUTATION BOUNDARY DOES NOT RESTATE IT. `stages/` already defines what a stage produces and `lib/stages.mjs` opens by warning that two hand-maintained descriptions of one pipeline disagree. A `mayCreate` list would be that second description, so there is none. (3) `mutationBoundary` NAMES CANONICAL NON-CREATION OPERATIONS. Its `mayMutate` entries are operation identifiers - the registry mutation keys plus `writeStageDocument`, `writeStageAttestation` and `setTypeActivation` - not artifact types and not tool wire names. It therefore says what a stage may CHANGE, while `produces` says what it may CREATE, and neither can be read as a weaker copy of the other. This still depends on TSK-0051, because the roster and the contracts it settled are what (1) is checked against.
